extracted.intended_audience: registrants' SEC reporting professionals, corporate accountants, and securities lawyers preparing business combination and acquisition disclosures (including investment companies and real estate transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which SEC and Reg S-X rules require financial statements or supplemental information when a registrant (including investment companies) acquires real estate, mortgage loans, funds, or other entities; how to test for significance and the periods/thresholds for required filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buyer’s continuing investment in real estate (ASC 360-20-40-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The buyer’s continuing investment in a real estate transaction shall not qualify unless the buyer is contractually required to pay each year on its total debt for the purchase price of the property an amount at least equal to the level annual payment that would be needed to pay that debt and interest on the unpaid balance over not more than (a) 20 years for debt for land and (b) the customary amortization term of a first mortgage loan by an independent established lending institution for other real estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ASC provision is used to assess whether an arrangement constitutes a continuing investment in real estate for SEC reporting purposes (and therefore may implicate S-X Rule 3-14).

rubrics_metrics.name: When Rule 3-14 requires acquired property financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-14 states that the financial statements of an acquired property should be furnished if the acquisition took place during the period for which the registrant’s income statements are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) of Rule 3-14 notes the information is not required to be included in a Form 10-K filing (consistent with Item 8 excluding acquired company financials that Rule 3-05 would otherwise require). The exceptions reflect that acquired properties/companies will generally be consolidated into registrant financials from acquisition date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant subsidiary threshold in Rule 3-09 (20% substitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-09(a) provides that if any of the conditions set forth in Rule 1-02(w) substituting 20 percent for 10 percent in the tests used therein to determine significant subsidiary are met, separate financial statements shall be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This substitution alters the numeric threshold used to determine when separate financial statements of subsidiaries (not consolidated) must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K requirement for acquired investment-type arrangements (10% threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: In filings on Form 8-K triggered in connection with an acquisition of an investment-type arrangement, separate audited financial statements are required for any such arrangement that individually constitutes 10% or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must evaluate whether an acquired investment-type arrangement meets the 10% significance trigger for separate audited statements in Form 8-K disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADC arrangement accounting and impact on required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition, Development, and Construction (ADC) arrangements are arrangements where a lender participates in residual profit from sale or refinancing and shares in the owner's risks and rewards; guidance determines whether a lender accounts for an ADC arrangement as a loan or as an investment in real estate or a joint venture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the loan is accounted for as an investment (or economic substance indicates investment/joint venture), SEC rules (e.g., S-X Rule 3-14) may require financial information of the underlying property securing mortgage loans. Consider whether arrangement conveys same risks/rewards as owner/joint venturer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which SEC rules can require property financial information (by accounting/economic substance)
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-09 and Rule 4-08(g) apply when the loan is accounted for as an investment that is not consolidated; S-X Rule 3-13 and Rule 408 apply when investment risks exist due to substantial asset concentration; S-X Rule 3-14 applies when the economic substance of the mortgage loans represents an investment in real estate or a joint venture rather than a loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisitions accounted as equity method investments are explicitly in the scope of S-X Rule 3-14. Use the accounting/economic-substance analysis to identify applicable S-X provisions for required disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file property financials at time of entering mortgage loan (ADC significant investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant enters into a significant ADC arrangement that is accounted for as an investment, financial statements of the underlying property securing the mortgage loan are filed under S-X Rule 3-14 in the Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because acquisitions of an interest in a real estate operation accounted as an equity method investment fall within S-X Rule 3-14(a)(2)(ii) and SAB Topic 1.I, registrants should include the underlying property financials in the Form 8-K when the ADC arrangement is significant and accounted as investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance determination for properties securing mortgage loans (10% vs 20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously the SEC staff stated property financials securing ADC loans are required in a registration statement when the amount loaned is 10% or more of the greater of registrant’s total assets or the offering proceeds. S-X Rule 3-14 was amended in 2020 to increase the significance threshold from 10% to 20%, but SAB Topic 1.I guidance referencing 10% remains unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the potential conflict between the 2020 amendment (20%) and prior SAB staff guidance (10%), registrants should consider consulting the SEC staff (CF-OCA) before applying the increased threshold to ADC loan acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement when mortgage loan not equity-method but asset concentration exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when a mortgage loan is not accounted for as an equity method investment, financial and other information may be required about properties securing mortgage loans if investment risks exist due to substantial asset concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, if over 20% of offering proceeds in a registration statement (or total assets at latest audited year-end, if greater) have been or will be invested in a single loan (or several related loans to same/affiliated borrowers), financial statements of the underlying property are required in both 1933 and 1934 Act filings. 'Related' properties include those subject to cross-default or collateralization agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of acquisitions of real estate subject to triple net leases
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of a lessee under a triple net lease would not meet the requirements of S-X Rule 3-14 to provide financial information of the acquired real estate operation(s); acquisitions of real estate operations subject to triple net leases are not treated differently from other acquisitions under S-X Rule 3-14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically registrants sometimes provided lessee financials when lessee considered significant, but the 2020 amendments clarified that lessee statements do not substitute for real estate operation statements. Separately, lessee financials may still be needed if the arrangement results in significant asset concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'fund' for S-X Rule 6-11 purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For S-X Rule 6-11, the term 'fund' includes: an investment company as defined in section 3(a) of the Investment Company Act of 1940 (including a BDC); a company that would be an investment company but for exclusions under sections 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7); or any private account managed by an investment adviser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 6-11 applies only to acquisitions of such 'funds' by investment company registrants; scope must be evaluated in light of facts and circumstances (e.g., acquisition of substantially all portfolio investments).

rubrics_metrics.name: When acquisition of multiple related funds is treated as a single acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions of a group of related funds that are probable or have occurred subsequent to the registrant’s latest fiscal year-end will be treated as a single acquisition if: (i) they are under common control or management; (ii) acquisition of one fund is conditional on acquisition of each other fund; or (iii) each acquisition is conditioned on a single common event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat related funds on a combined basis for significance and filing determinations under S-X Rule 6-11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of significance for acquired funds (investment test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment test: total value of the registrant’s (and subsidiaries’) investments in and advances to the acquired fund compared to >20% of the value of the registrant’s total investments (consolidated) from most recent annual financial statements; if >20%, the acquired fund is significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC uses total investments (not total assets) to focus on investment-portfolio impact; for S-X Rule 6-11 the 20% substitution is used for the investment-company-specific significance test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of significance for acquired funds (income test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Income test (Reg S-X Rule 1-02(w)(2)(ii)): the absolute value of combined investment income, net realized gains/losses, and net change in unrealized gains/losses from the tested subsidiary for the most recently completed fiscal year is compared to (A) 80% of the absolute value of the change in net assets from operations of the registrant, or (B) 10% of that change and the investment test condition exceeds 5%; five-year averaging may be used in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of S-X Rule 6-11, if significance exceeds 20% under either test, financial statements must be filed. The 'primary income test' under S-X Rule 1-02(w)(2)(ii)(A) is not applied for S-X Rule 6-11 purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate-significance (50%) and periods to present under S-X Rule 6-11
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 6-11(b)(2) requires substituting 20% for 10% when determining whether financial statements and supplemental information are required; if none of the substituted 20% conditions are satisfied, statements are not required. If any substituted 20% condition is satisfied, file the fund’s financials (most recent fiscal year and most recent interim period) and supplemental information. If the aggregate impact of funds acquired since the latest audited registrant balance sheet (for which statements are not required individually) satisfies the substituted 50% condition, the registrant must provide financial statements for any such fund(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combined comparison to registrant’s most recent annual financial statements filed at or prior to the acquisition; pro forma amounts may be used in certain cases where prior acquired fund statements and supplemental info were filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for performing significance tests (which statements to compare)
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance determination is made by comparing the most recent annual financial statement of each fund (or combined group for related funds) to the registrant’s most recent annual financial statements filed at or prior to the date of acquisition. Pro forma amounts may be used in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant filed audited financials of a fund acquired after its latest fiscal year-end and provided required supplemental information, subsequent acquisitions’ significance tests may use pro forma amounts giving effect to the previous acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine whether a 'fund' acquisition has occurred or is probable
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination requires evaluating all facts and circumstances (legal form is not determinative). Consider whether the transaction results in acquisition of all or substantially all portfolio investments of another fund and other specific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEC staff considerations (not an exhaustive checklist) include: how it was determined that acquisition equates to less than substantially all; the transaction’s business purpose; relationship between parties; future operating plans of selling fund; whether investors will move to registrant; whether selling fund’s management will be involved post-transaction; how purchase affects registrant strategy; whether transaction seeds the registrant or is warehousing. Assessing probability includes analyzing progress, penalties for failure, and significance of regulatory approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: when S-X Rule 6-11 applies vs non-fund acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 6-11 applies when an investment company registrant acquires a 'fund' as defined in the Rule. For non-fund acquisitions, investment company registrants must follow S-X Rule 3-05 and Article 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See other chapters for application of S-X Rule 3-05/Article 11; correctly identifying whether an acquisition is a 'fund' acquisition is critical to applying the proper reporting rules.
